newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Aznar urges parties to labour reform.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar urges parties to labour reform.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said on Tuesday that the government would not stand by and simply watch unions and businessmen spar over an accord on labour contracts that further the creation of employment.

"The government cannot be held apart from the terms of the agreement. An agreement where everything remains as is would not be sufficient. In a matter of such importance for the development of the country, the government...will act accordingly," Aznar said at an economic summit on Spain.
Aznar added that talks between unions and businessmen, which are due to begin at the start of 1997, should lead to solutions "that provide guarantees for business and workers."
He said "we cannot continue to understand labour contracts as a fight between workers and employers. We have to find useful, stable, nimble formulas."
Aznar added that the reformist spirit of his government will not shrink from carrying out as many structural reforms as are necessary.
